content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Green Bay

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and documented project-management experience. Review PMI's specific requirements for your background—secondary diploma holders and bachelor's degree holders face different thresholds. Granite PM Academy's advisors can quickly verify whether you meet PMI's criteria before you invest in training.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Instruction
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual PMP Boot Camp, taught by experienced instructors who deliver the full PMI curriculum in real time. Attend sessions on your schedule—evenings and weekends available for Green Bay professionals. Upon completion, you'll receive a certificate of training required for your PMI application.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After earning your contact hours, create your PMI account and formally apply for the PMP credential. Upload your education and experience documentation, then pay the PMI exam fee directly to the Project Management Institute. Granite PM Academy staff can guide you through the online submission process.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice exams, study guides, and Q&A sessions—to build confidence before test day. Schedule your computer-based exam through PMI's testing partner at a local Green Bay testing center. Our instructors remain available to clarify difficult concepts during your final weeks of study.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your Credential
steps_items.text: Once certified, you'll renew your PMP every three years by earning Professional Development Units (PDUs) through approved learning activities, training, and project work. Granite PM Academy offers PDU-eligible courses and workshops to help you stay current and keep your credential active throughout your career.
